Mubadala Energy is pleased to launch the fifth publication of our annual Sustainability Report, which highlights our performance, efforts, and forward plan regarding our material environmental, social and governance (ESG) topics for 2023. We are committed to responsibly providing energy to meet growing global energy demand, ensuring that in the process, we not only deliver on our targets to our shareholder, but we also positively impact the environment and societies in which we do business. The parameters within which this report was prepared are outlined to the right:

This report captures data based on a detailed list of sustainability topics for the period January 1st to December 31st, 2023. The report has been prepared in accordance with several sustainability reporting standards, including the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) 2021 Revised Universal Standards, the GRI 2021 Oil and Gas Sector Specific Standards, and the 2020 International Petroleum Industry Environmental Conservation Association (IPIECA) Sustainability Reporting Guidance. Our disclosures cover issues that are most material to our business and its stakeholders, with these areas clearly identified through a transparent materiality assessment process. In this year's assessment we have considered the 'double materiality' methodology, derived from the 2023 European Union's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), and other related methodologies. We also incorporate where applicable, the recommendations outlined in the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), covering the significant strides we have made in terms of our action on climate change around our strategy, governance, and action plan around reducing our greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions profile. Finally, we remain committed to supporting global sustainability initiatives, and included in this report are our contributions towards achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs). We are also committed to supporting the national ambitions of the countries in which we do business and highlight in this report our relevant contributions. All environmental and safety metrics in this report align with the operational control method of reporting, covering our operated activities in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand. In cases where investments or divestments were made, we report within the period operatorship was held. All other data presented in this report is representative of 100% of Mubadala Energy's business, unless otherwise specified. For this year' s reporting, we have completed an independent assurance of our Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions for our operated assets (UAE, Indonesia, Malaysia) for the calendar years' 2022 and 2023. Our Thailand operated assets are not included due to the completion of divestment of these assets in Q1'2023. Our GHG emissions Reporting Criteria for Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions are also included in this year' s report for reference. We welcome any comments or feedback on our 2023 Sustainability Report: Communications@mubadalaenergy.com Our current and past sustainability reports can also be found on our website: www.mubadalaenergy.com

It is with great pleasure that we launch Mubadala Energy's fifth annual sustainability report, which highlights the key sustainability issues we confront as a company, and the progress we have made over the last year in positively impacting these areas.' Mansoor Mohamed Al Hamed Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Mubadala Energy Sustainability Report 2023

I am immensely proud of the progress we delivered in 2023 on the material environmental, social and governance (ESG) areas we monitor and actively manage. Our strategy is now fully in motion, and we have firmly embedded the principles of the energy transition as the foundation of our business. Our portfolio exposure to gas has expanded in the last year, from 66% in 2022 to almost 69% of our overall working interest production of 369kboe/d in 2023, as we recognize the importance of gas as a low carbon solution particularly in the regions where we do business. As we look to the future, our coverage and growth across the gas value chain is anticipated to continue, and we are pleased to have also shared updates on our recent exploration successes in countries like Indonesia. The Layaran-1 discovery in our operated assets in South Andaman which was announced in 2023 paves the way to support Indonesia's decarbonization ambitions. This focus on expanding across low carbon energy solutions permeates throughout our global portfolio of assets, as we recognize the critical importance of responsibly managing and reducing our emissions footprint, supporting our contribution to national and international climate targets.

In the year that coincided with the UAE hosting the UNFCCC's COP28 event in Dubai, we were also able to make significant strides in reducing our emissions footprint. Last year alone, we delivered a 66% reduction in our Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, which takes our average GHG emissions intensity down from 35.2 kgCO 2 e/boe in 2022, to an average of 15.3 kgCO 2 e/boe in 2023. This is a testament to the firm focus and commitment that we have made as an organization to the responsible provision of energy. Not only are we actively managing our global portfolio of assets, but also introducing the right interventions, whether it be technology or process optimizations, to improve our performance. In so doing, we continue to align with the climate ambitions of our shareholder, the UAE, and of the countries where we do business, contributing towards the achievement of Net Zero targets.

content_text: We see partnerships in these areas as a key to success, as the scale of expansion in these areas to meaningfully impact global climate ambitions requires close collaboration by all key stakeholders - from energy producers to technology providers, regulators, policy makers, and consumers. Our energy transition efforts extend to our social contribution programs too. I am proud of the commitment we announced in 2023 to plant 700,000 mangrove trees here in Abu Dhabi over the next seven years. We have also expanded our efforts in biodiversity as key carbon sinks to other areas of our global portfolio. This important commitment, which is also part of our pledge signed with the Environmental Agency - Abu Dhabi, will contribute to the UAE's overall commitment of planting 100 million mangrove trees by 2030.

The significant progress we have made along these, and other ESG areas, could not have been possible without two main priorities for our business. Firstly, an unwavering commitment to health and safety of anyone who works with us, and secondly, cultivating a team of highly dedicated and motivated employees who live the values of Mubadala Energy day-in and day-out. In 2023, we recorded zero lost time injuries (LTI) across our entire portfolio of operated assets. In our Ruby operated gas field in Indonesia, we marked a key milestone in 2023 of zero LTIs since operations started in 2013, an impeccable 10year record. Our team, along with the continuous support of our shareholder and Board of Directors, are the heart of our success and I extend my sincerest gratitude to all for our achievements over the last year. 2023 was a year where Mubadala Energy put its Transformation in Action , and we look forward to progressing our sustainability journey even further in the coming years ahead.

Driving the energy transition at the speed and scale needed to deliver on our national and international climate ambitions is a tremendously broad challenge, but one that also presents immense opportunity. It requires the commitment of not only the wide spectrum of energy producers, but also of host governments, policy makers, technology providers and energy consumers to ensure successful and timely progress. Mubadala Energy's focused approach to the energy transition and commitment to responsible growth underpins our delivery of long-term value creation for our shareholder, alongside our dedication to being a partner of choice within our wider stakeholder group. We are deeply committed to fulfilling our role as a sustainable energy provider in all countries where we do business. - Read more about our strategy on our website. Informed by an extensive assessment of current and future market dynamics, our 2030 strategy is underpinned by three key realities: - The energy transition is accelerating change within our industry, with natural gas positioned as a key bridging fuel to a lower carbon future - ESG considerations have evolved as a major driver of investment decisions for all industries, including ours - Our shareholder, Mubadala, has committed to accelerating progress in both areas

content_text: We pay close attention to the risks posed by climate change to our business, and hence our strategic investment and growth pillars are based on the responsible and sustainable provision of energy. We recognize the opportunities presented through the expansion of focus on low carbon solutions, and alignment to the UAE's Net Zero by 2050 target as well as the climate ambitions of the countries in which we do business. As we deliver on our mission to become a resilient, low-carbon energy company, we are fully committed to reducing our Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions in line with international standards. Last year was pivotal for Mubadala Energy; we doubled down on our strategic objective of growing our presence across the gas value chain, whilst exploring new energy opportunities in geothermal energy, carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS), and blue hydrogen. These pillars of growth within our strategy stand firmly in their contribution towards the energy transition, and our core capabilities and experience position us for expansion in these areas. We saw the share natural gas increase in our overall working interest production in 2023, growing from 63 to 69 percent over the last three years (2021 - 2023). The divestment of mature oil assets in Thailand and ramp up of production from our operated Pegaga gas field in Malaysia's SK320, contributed to this increased gas weighting within our portfolio, and to the reduction in our overall emissions intensity. In the regions where we operate such as Southeast Asia, coal-fired power is still a major part of the energy mix, and the transition to lower-carbon fuels such as gas is critical to meeting Net Zero ambitions.

Natural gas is positioned to be a key enabler of the energy transition, particularly in its role to achieve faster decarbonization through accelerating the phase-out of coal. Gas-fired power plants have the potential to reduce carbon emissions by 50 - 60 percent compared to coal-powered alternatives, whilst also generating power more efficiently. Coal-to-gas substitution can make a significant contribution in a Net-Zero roadmap, where coal in the global energy system currently accounts for around 40% of the world' s energy-related GHG emissions. Mubadala Energy first introduced our Sustainability Framework in 2020, highlighting the critical role ESG considerations make to our corporate strategy and the underlying philosophy of how we do business. Our sustainability mission is clear and simple: We seek to connect the opportunities of the energy transition with our ambitions towards creating a positive environmental, social and economic impact.

This Framework rests on three pillars, which have been embedded across all functions within our organization, and are factored into our key decisions: - Taking Positive Environmental Action: Taking bold steps in alignment with national and global sustainability agendas. - Being the Partner of Choice: Continuously improving our sustainability performance and generating value to our stakeholders. - Delivering Responsible Operations: Setting the tone from the top and integrating sustainability across every facet of our business. Together, these pillars reflect our commitment to addressing material and relevant ESG risks that are applicable to our business, while harnessing the opportunities offered by the energy transition. All key ESG activities we undertake as an organization are also mapped based on their alignment and contribution to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs). - For more detail, please see page 63.

In 2022, we rolled out our first Sustainability Strategy, which helped to integrate the overarching pillars of our Sustainability Framework into every facet of our business. In terms of understanding the relevant ESG focus areas for our entire portfolio, we have targeted two main foundational areas: - 1) How do we develop, enhance and sustain resilient operations - this requires a continued robust focus on areas such as health and safety, the environment, people who work for and on behalf of us, and the communities we impact. - 2) How do we identify and pursue investments in sustainable new ventures - this includes having the right frameworks and structures in place to support responsible investing, including a careful approach to partner selection and engagement. The strategic enablers of these two main areas include the underlying policies, processes, and systems we have in place, our governance frameworks, an ongoing process of alignment with our key stakeholders, and ensuring that as we transition to a more sustainable business, we have a team with the right capabilities on hand to enable progress.

In alignment with one of the key pillars of our sustainability framework, we seek to have a positive contribution on the environment through our activities, and the nature of our industry necessitates that environmental considerations are some of the top material issues we consider. We have a long history of conducting our business in a manner that protects and conserves the environment. Our approach to environmental protection is aligned with the UAE's firm ambitions to mitigate global climate change risks. We have also built over many years a proven track record of complying with, and exceeding the regulatory requirements associated with our operations, utilizing technology and innovative solutions where needed to ensure we operate responsibly and efficiently.

Every business unit within our operated portfolio of assets must execute our Operations Management System (OMS) and Environmental Management Standard (EMS), which guide our efforts towards making a purposeful environmental impact. Together, they outline the framework for operational best practices that help us proactively identify and mitigate potential environmental risks, and cover all aspects of air pollution, waste management, water and energy use, and biodiversity impacts. The OMS and EMS are governed by our Quality, Health, Safety, Security and Environment (QHSSE) Policy. As part of a comprehensive risk management strategy, to ensure our OMS and EMS capture the most relevant industry guidelines, it is reviewed annually and updated as required. The EMS in all our operated business units (Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand) are certified to ISO 14 001:2015 (Environmental Management System), ISO 9001:2015 (Quality Management System), and ISO 45001: 2018 (Occupational Health and Safety Management System) in 2023. In addition, we also ensure compliance with country-specific requirements, and are subject to oversight from relevant regulatory bodies in the countries where we do business. Oversight also includes periodic audits from our shareholder, to ensure that we remain aligned with international best practices. In 2023, our Indonesia Business Unit received for a fourth consecutive year the Green rating for PROPER audit conducted by Indonesia's Ministry of Environment and Forestry (MOEF). PROPER is a mandatory audit conducted yearly by MOEF to assess environmental performance in terms of regulatory compliance in areas such as energy efficiency, emission reduction, water and wastewater reduction, hazardous and nonhazardous waste reduction, biodiversity, and community development. A Green rating indicates that the company has implemented environmental management procedures above the standards set by the Ministry.

As we deliver on our mission as low-carbon energy producer, we are fully committed to reducing our GHG emissions in line with our QHSSE and ESG Policies, Operating Management System, and Environmental Management Standards. In terms of the calculation and reporting of emissions, our internally developed GHG Calculation and Reporting Guidelines is aligned with international standards and best practice. In this year's report, we disclose our Scope 1 and 2 emissions reporting criteria in the Appendix. We have a deep understanding of the risks posed by climate change, and we are dedicated to minimizing these risks through the implementation of our energy transition strategy that aligns closely with the sustainability agenda of our shareholder, the UAE government and the host nations in which we operate. Following the outcomes of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) discussions at the 28th Conference of Parties (COP28), we continue to explore enhancements and innovations that will support the decarbonization of our operations, and investments in new energy areas that will facilitate the provision of lower carbon energy sources to the key markets in which we do business, supporting the climate targets of such countries. Specifically in 2023, the impact of our ongoing strategy implementation and portfolio optimization efforts bore fruit, with the achievement of a 66% reduction in our Scope 1 & 2 emissions This also translated into a 57% reduction in our Scope 1 & Scope 2 emissions intensity compared to our 2022 footprint, with a reduction from 35.2 tons kgCO 2 e/ boe in 2022 to 15.3 tons kgCO 2 e/boe in 2023. This performance aligns us with our industry peers who are ranked top tier based on their progress in this area and leading the charge in terms of emissions management. Excluding our Thailand operated assets which were divested in early 2023, our 2022 and 2023 Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions have been independently assured (please refer to the Appendix for the Assurance Statement). Although our 2023 results can be partially attributed to the divestment of our Thailand operated oil positions, this performance also indicates that our innovation and enhancement projects in decarbonizing our operations across our global portfolio are making a difference. Examples of such enhancements introduced in 2023 include:

- Reducing the running hours of air compressor usage on our Ruby offshore platform by around 800 hours - Installing fuel treatment devices on heat exchangers used during drilling operations, resulting in more than 20% reduction in both CO2 and NOX emissions - Utilizing biodiesel during drilling operations, which not only reduces our CO2 footprint, but is also more cost effective - Installing outdoor lighting photocells which have halved outdoor lighting requirements, reducing our energy consumption

- Implementing 'smart' or digital GHG measurement, monitoring and reporting on the Pegaga offshore platform which helps us to access real-time data, and accelerate interventions - Managing flaring in strict compliance with the regulatory limits set forth in the Petronas Minimum Environmental Standards - Exploring the use of GHG cameras and drones to measure fugitive emissions and improve reporting.

In addition to our GHG emissions, we monitor and address wider air emissions and pollutants. In the last year, we recorded a significant reduction in volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions as well as nitrogen oxide (NOX). The reductions in VOC's and NOX, while in part due to our divestment from Thailand operations, indicate the success of the technological interventions we introduced in our operations. Reductions in flaring and venting are two key priorities our industry continues to place emphasis on, and importantly so. In 2023, our volume of flared gas reduced by 62%, and our total venting reduced by 76%. In our Indonesia drilling operations, the installation of fuel treatment devices on heat exchangers significantly contributed to the reduction in our flaring. In Malaysia, we continue to manage a strict flaring practice in adherence to the regulatory limits set by local authorities, ensuring that our operations meet the minimum environmental standards set forth. Our management practices are governed by our QHSSE Policy and Environmental Management Standards. In 2023, we implemented numerous energy efficiency and innovation initiatives, and alongside our Thailand assets' divestments, these led to a near 46% reduction in energy consumption compared to our 2022 performance. Our direct energy consumption, which accounted for approximately 99% of our overall energy usage, totaled around 2.7 million GJ. The primary source of this consumption was diesel fuel utilized in the generators powering our offshore facilities. Energy efficiency enhancements in our Indonesia business unit included the change-out of outdoor lighting installations, which cut the running hours of outdoor lighting systems from 24 to 12 hours. Our flexible working for employees also translates to optimized air conditioning and lighting usage in our offices. Our Malaysia office in Kuala Lumpur is partially powered by solar power, although the impact of this is not reported. Reduction in Total Energy Consumption within our operating assets in 2023 46%

We strive to reduce our water consumption across our onshore and offshore facilities. This commitment entails identifying and implementing innovative approaches to enhance operational efficiency, while minimizing wastewater generation. In 2023, our total freshwater consumption declined by ca. 86%, driven mainly by the exclusion of our Thailand oil assets which were divested early in the year. An increased rate of freshwater recycling to almost 16% for the year was also the result of lower freshwater consumption. The increased drilling activities in our Indonesia business unit however contributed to an increase in seawater consumption by around 31%, and hence an increase in our overall water consumption intensity from 20.1 m3/kboe in 2022, to 32.4 m3/kboe in 2023. We continue to deploy technologies and best practices to conserve, reuse and recycle precious water resources. For example, in our Indonesia business unit, we have launched the water clarifier injection program to remove oil from wastewater. The clarifier stimulates hydrocarbon floc growth and, in turn, enables hydrocarbon separation from wastewater. We are also reusing water from air conditioning units based on a detailed Life Cycle Assessment and adjusting laundry cycles in our facilities for greater efficiency. In Abu Dhabi, we marked World Water Day in March with an employee campaign comprising simple water-saving tips - from buying locally and seasonally, to taking part in wetland conservation. In our Indonesia business unit, we marked four consecutive years of achieving the 'Green' PROPER rating by the Ministry of Environment and Forestry. These rigorous audits are conducted annually to assess environmental performance in terms of compliance (or above) on areas including wastewater reduction. Our Waste Management System, which is ISO14001-certified, follows the guidelines set by the International Maritime Organization and complies with local regulations where applicable. This comprehensive system covers various aspects of waste management, including hazardous waste, nonhazardous waste, recyclable materials, and biological waste, across our assets, offshore facilities, offices, and warehouses. In 2023, we had a ca. 20% reduction in overall waste generated, with a total of 442 tons. Our total waste intensity remained stable as measured by tons of waste generated per thousand barrels of oil equivalent of production. Around 3% of our total waste generated was also recycled last year. We provide regular communication on waste and resource efficiency, including annual awareness campaigns to employees. In Abu Dhabi, for example, we have improved office recycling facilities and signage and employee awareness around the need to 'reduce, reuse, recycle' , with a particular emphasis on single-use plastics. We have transitioned to recycled materials in our canteen packaging, coffee cups, sleeves and lids and printing paper. In our Indonesia business unit, a hazardous waste reduction program focused on the used air filters in 2023 - the aim being to separate non-hazardous waste from used filters (Filter Enclosure Separation Program). The programme led to a reduction of around 0.16 of used filter waste for the year. Across our business units, we have robust and comprehensive systems in place to prevent leakages of oil, water and other substances from our equipment and facilities. According to our reporting guidelines, we are obligated to report spills exceeding 1 barrel in volume. We are proud to report zero reportable spills to date. This is testament to the efficacy and enforcement of our QHSSE policy and Environmental Management Standards, as well as the diligence of our global workforce.

As most of our operations are conducted offshore, our biodiversity initiatives are primarily centered around marine conservation, scientific research, and education. Importantly, we seek to uphold the strategic priorities outlined by the leadership of the UAE, including the Abu Dhabi Climate Change Strategy. One prominent example is our focus on mangrove planting, which presents multiple benefits, including climate change mitigation, coastal protection, water quality improvement, and the provision of essential habitats for diverse species. At the UNFCCC's COP27 held in Egypt, the UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) announced the launch of the Mangrove Alliance for Climate (MAC), which seeks to support, enhance and expand mangrove forests globally as a nature-based solution against climate disruptions. Following this, the UAE's MOCCAE announced at the end of 2022 the target to plant 100 million mangrove tress across the country by 2030, as an important contributor to blue carbon projects. As part of our biodiversity initiatives, we have channeled significant efforts in the last year to align and incorporate this agenda through our activities, and in 2023 we announced our first biodiversity target for the UAE of planting 700,000 mangrove trees by 2030. In 2023 we announced our first biodiversity target for the UAE of planting 700,000 mangrove trees by 2030

In 2023, Mubadala Energy became among the first organizations in the UAE to sign the Abu Dhabi Environment Agency's (EAD) Abu Dhabi Mangroves Initiative (ADMI) Pledge, with a commitment to plant 700,000 mangroves in Abu Dhabi by 2030, equivalent to an annual target of 100,000 trees per year until 2030. This Pledge establishes a framework to help conserve and restore mangroves and other blue carbon ecosystems in the UAE and globally and aims to recognize the huge impact of nature-based solutions that these ecosystems provide, while helping accelerate their conservation and restoration through sciencebacked research and innovation. In line with this, we have started work to harness innovative drone and mapping technology to ensure the most effective planting program.

content_text: In 2022, our Indonesia business unit commenced the construction of a green-house project in one of our local community areas (Hilir Muara village). This project will serve as a nursery area for Kalimantan's endemic and endangered plant species such as Mangifera Casturi and the Durio Dulcis. The project will also support planting of several crops with economic value with hydroponic system (due to limited land space) that is targeted to improve the welfare of local communities. The construction was completed in 2022 and it is fully operated by community by mid-2023. This program has increased the biodiversity index within the Hilir Muara Village, and successfully supports growth of 27 plant species, with three of these species being native Kalimantan region and with endangered or vulnerable status from International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).

content_text: In Indonesia, Mubadala Energy has achieved in 2023 the coveted PROPER Green Rating for a fourth consecutive year. The Program for Pollution Control, Evaluation and Rating (PROPER) is a mandatory audit conducted each year by the Indonesian Ministry of Environment and Forestry. It assesses environmental performance and compliance with regulatory requirements, including energy efficiency, reductions in emissions, water and waste, biodiversity, and community development. The program is built on the premise that public disclosure and accountability, transparency in operations, and community participation will foster more sustainable practices by organizations to achieve effective and sustained pollution control. In 2023, we have exceeded the required standards with multiple initiatives that we have delivered, some examples of which include: - Emissions reduction via the use of lower emitting fuels in our operations processes - Energy efficiency enhancements via installation of more efficient lighting systems - Waste management via the use of Filter Enclosure Separation program to reduce hazardous waste - Water management via the Water Clarifier Injection Program which reduces produced waste-water load to the sea - Biodiversity projects such as infrastructure development to support the regeneration of endemic and endangered plants We remain committed to maintaining this outstanding rating.

Embedded in our DNA as a company is our unwavering commitment to safeguarding the wellbeing and safety of everyone who conducts work on our behalf, including our employees and contractors. This commitment exists at every level of our organization and has allowed us to maintain our top-quartile safety performance which we continue to receive recognition for across our industry.

Our safety culture is built on the approach of anticipating, preparing, and preventing, with the primary goal of eliminating any operational incidents. This mandates that potential risks must be identified, controlled, and mitigated at the outset of every operation, with this proactive risk management approach creating a safer working environment for everyone. Governed by our Quality, Health, Safety, Security and Environment (QHSSE) Policy, our safety culture empowers every member of our team, including contractors, to stop operations if they notice any safety concerns. Our Vision Zero Safety Campaign is reinforced by our ultimate objective is to ensure a daily record of zero recordable incidents , and we believe that cooperation and continuous learning are key to achieving this goal. Our top priority is to continuously enhance our safety performance yearly. In 2023, we recorded 3.22 million working hours completed by our employees and contractors, with a consistent record of zero fatalities across all our areas of operations, and we remain steadfast in ensuring this important safety record is maintained. In addition, we had a total recordable injury rate (TRIR), and a lost-time injury rate (LTIR) of zero across all our operated assets in 2023, an achievement we are immensely proud to report. Specifically, in our Ruby operations in Indonesia, we have celebrated in 2023 ten years of zero LTI, spanning the period of the beginning of the field's operations to current date. Also, in our Pegaga operations in Malaysia, the end of 2023 marked two years without LTI. Through our performance over the years, we recognize that, given the nature of our operations, how we conduct the engagement and onboarding of our contractors remains key to ensuring our safety culture is upheld. We thoroughly investigate every safety incident and conduct root cause analyses to identify any underlying causes to help enhance our performance in the future. We also implement effective measures to mitigate future risks and prevent similar incidents from occurring.

Occupational safety campaigns in our Indonesia business unit included injury prevention at sites, and the delivery of our internally-developed 'Take HEARRT' training - Hazard Elimination and Risk Reduction Training - for new hired and drilling contractors to support our drilling campaign in our North Sumatra exploration licenses which were conducted in 2023. We provide competitive reward and compensation packages, along with a wide array of benefits, including flexible working arrangements, parental leave (for men and women), remote working options, exceptional leave policies, seniority awards, mental and physical health support, and Employee Assistance Programs. This includes a knowledge sharing workshop held with a wide range of colleagues from Pertamina Persero to discuss ESG and energy transition, digitalization, strategic pivots, etc.

With 31 nationalities across our organization, establishing and sustaining a work environment where everyone has an equal opportunity to representation and engagement with the provision of safety and respect is an unwavering commitment to diversity and non-discrimination. content_text: Being a Partner of Choice includes building a sustainable and progressive relationship with our staff. The company also encourages the following development approach a) On-The-Job Training (OJT) and b) Coaching & Mentoring. This is to ensure that development effectiveness is also managed. We conduct an annual talent management process that involves talent reviews, mapping, and succession planning to develop future leaders for our evolving business needs. We also have a Young Engineers Program designed for new graduates that combines on-the-job and classroom training over two years, with a focus on developing technical and core competency skills to help them succeed in their careers. Courses which were administered across our business units in 2023 ranged from leadership skills, change management and financial wellbeing, to GHG measurement, waste management and energy transition topics. Our goal is to make a positive and lasting impact for our shareholder, society, and the environment by acting as a responsible citizen in the communities where we do business. Through our Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) strategy, we drive focused projects across four main strategic priorities: Environment, Employee Engagement, Education, and Community Development. Our Community Investment Policy was updated in 2023 to fully reflect these priorities. In 2023, we invested more than AED 2 million to support 26 CSR projects in UAE, Malaysia and Indonesia, reaching over 58,000 beneficiaries. 2023 was a hallmark year for Mubadala Energy, as this was declared as the 'Y ear of Sustainability' by the leadership of the UAE, and the year in which the UNFCCC's COP28 was held in Dubai. Therefore, in line with the four pillars of our CSR Framework, we expanded our environmental and sustainability investments with a particular focus on mangrove conservation and protection, an important naturebased lever in decarbonization efforts. Employee engagement in CSR continued in 2023, with a range of activities and projects conducted across our global operations. Overall, 60 employee volunteers gave over 330 hours to local community causes. Beneficiaries of our CSR Projects in 2023
CSR projects must create meaningful and sustainable change that improves people's lives. To ensure this, we carefully oversee all projects, planning to execution and evaluation: 1.

We identify projects that align with our strategic vision and involve actively engaging with stakeholders through diverse channels. We conduct rigorous Ethics and Compliance due diligence. We engage third-party experts to craft a detailed roadmap for action. 2.

We regularly review progress to ensure quality and effectiveness and we evaluate key projects' impact on local communities, considering stakeholder satisfaction and other factors such as the number of beneficiaries supported. Each business unit follows a distinct process to measure impact against the UN SDGs. We also conduct an annual review process to ensure that projects remain aligned with the evolving needs and aspirations of the communities we serve. In 2023, we established a stakeholder engagement procedure and stakeholder grievance process. In some instances, we work closely with NonGovernmental Organizations (NGOs) to identify the most vulnerable communities in targeted areas. Once we obtain internal approvals for our CSR initiatives, we outline the scope of responsibilities between our relevant business unit, and the selected NGO. Each unit's communications team will work closely with the chosen NGO to receive regular updates in a timely manner until the project's completion. To ensure project effectiveness, we have initiated an additional layer of project assurance by conducting a post-CSR project visit to ensure that all investments were channeled to the identified group of communities. We also conduct a postproject impact assessment to ensure we have achieved the targets for each programme. 3.
We institutionalize successful projects and communicate to stakeholders and communities.

With 2023 being marked as the Year of Sustainability by the leadership of the UAE, we focused particularly on environmental projects. We announced our first biodiversity target in October 2023 - with a commitment to plant 700,000 mangrove trees in Abu Dhabi over the next 7 years, in line with the UAE' s overall target of planting 100 million mangroves by 2030. We began to forge new partnerships to enhance our impact, such as our partnership with Distant Imagery, a UAE-based company specializing in using drone technology to map and plant mangroves. We continued to support other tree-planting initiatives, as well as the creation of artificial reefs, turtle/sea crab protection projects, waste management schemes, and educational programs focused on environmental conservation and climate impact. Additionally, we also provided support for programs that aim to improve the use of renewable energy in the communities we serve. And we expanded our environmental conservation work through beach clean-ups and educational presentations at Abu Dhabi schools.

In Indonesia, we have been working to help communities in Kotabaru build knowledge around sustainable environmental practices for the last five years. In this region, pressures on land and marine resources are threatening ecosystems and exacerbating food insecurity. The multistakeholder Ecogreen program trains and supports women and young people to cultivate nutritional vegetables in their own homes. Impacting 20 households in 2022, the program now involves 50 households across eight neighborhoods (mainly fishing communities) and includes hydroponic planting and a nursery for endemic and endangered plants, including three endangered species on the International Union for the Conservation of Nature's (IUCN) Red List of threatened species. Ecogreen has also reduced waste by avoiding consumption of packaged, process foods.

We provide support for various educational initiatives, which include offering scholarships to financially disadvantaged students, organizing skills training programs, and making improvements to school facilities in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Abu Dhabi.

Our CSR partnerships in Malaysia include efforts to support the local communities in Sarawak in the enhancement of social well-being and development. In 2023, we sponsored four postgraduate students from Malaysia's Asia School of Business to conduct a CSR market survey in Bintulu, Sarawak. The purpose of the survey was to study and explore potential community initiatives that we can implement in Malaysia based on thorough research and engagement with Bintulu's community, taking into consideration the community demographic and social-economic activities. This 'action learning' sought to gain a deeper understanding of local socioeconomic challenges and identify potential assistance opportunities. Through collaborations with world class universities, we aim to provide students with strategic insights into the CSR investment landscape where we operate, while sharpening our own stakeholder mapping to determine future community investments and help build deeper connections with the local community.

We collaborate with local stakeholders, including community groups, NGOs, and local authorities, to provide financial and non-financial support. In this way, we gain a clear understanding of the needs of the local communities so that we can provide assistance that is meaningful and sustainable.

Among the nine CSR Projects we operate in Indonesia is a program to tackle malnutrition and stunted growth in children - a tragic reality affecting some toddlers of underprivileged families in the Kotabaru region of South Kalimantan. According to the World Health Organization, the most effective intervention is to support breastfeeding in the first six months of life, and thereafter to help children consume healthy, highquality nutrient-rich foods. Our program not only provides nutritional food and supplements to at-risk children, but it mentors parents to provide the best start in life. In just 90 days of this intervention, the results can be seen in childhood weight and height development - with children gaining up to 5cm in height and 1 kilogram in weight. What's more, their nutrient consumption nears the median number for children of the same age group.

In 2023, our Malaysian office sponsored new medical equipment for the pediatric ward at Bintulu Hospital in Sarawak. The new equipment will assist doctors and medical staff to more accurately monitor vital signs and administer medication for children diagnosed with cancer. We have also sponsored the hospital's playground refurbishment and donated five air purifier units to the Sarawak Children's Cancer Society halfway home in Kuching. Meanwhile, in conjunction with Malaysia's 66th Independence Day, we supported food aid distribution to 450 underprivileged families in the Sarawak districts of Kuching, Bintulu, Miri, and Sibu. Priority was given to low-income, single mothers caring for young children, the sick, elderly, and differently-abled communities, regardless of their background, race, and ethnicity.

Mubadala Energy is proud to be one of the founding partners in the Beyond2020 humanitarian initiative, which was launched by the Zayed Sustainability Prize in 2019, with the aim of furthering the humanitarian legacy of the UAE's Founding Father, Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, by providing sustainable technologies and solutions to vulnerable communities around the world. Malaysia marks the 17th deployment of the initiative, which provided improved access to clean water for 10,000 community members in Sabah and Sarawak regions of Malaysia, along the Rajang River. The people there have traditionally relied on surface water from the river for drinking and subsistence. Without the proper technology and systems to treat the water, villagers often experienced health issues. The solution was designed by Wateroam, the 2022 Zayed Sustainability Prize winner in the Water category, who implemented sustainable water fountains in 25 rural Malaysian villages to provide clean, safe water, reducing waterborne illnesses.

We believe that transparent and ethical governance practices are essential to ensuring business stability and continuity, whilst maintaining our value proposition. As a wholly owned subsidiary of Mubadala, we have a clearly defined governance structure, and where applicable, we adhere to the policies of our shareholder to ensure the highest standards are upheld without compromising our commitment to integrity and applicable laws. Establishing and enforcing clear governance frameworks and policies underpins our sustainability ambitions to be a partner of choice, wherein we embed transparency, ethical practices, and fairness into all our activities. The scale and nature of our business and the contribution we make to our shareholder's value proposition necessitates that the relationship between Mubadala Energy and our shareholder is clearly defined. A Delegation of Authority defines the authority granted to Mubadala Energy by our shareholder to execute our strategy, including new investments, and progression of projects. In terms of our governance structure, the Board of Directors (Board) appointed by our shareholder provides the direction and oversight on the strategic priorities for our business, and guides our performance based on the implementation of these priorities. Mubadala Energy's Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is accountable to the Board for all aspects of the company's business, including its governance. The Executive Committee (ExCom), established by the Board of Directors, is entrusted with certain delegated authority and responsibilities which include the preparation of our strategic plan, providing risk oversight and setting the ethical 'tone on the top' .

Mubadala Energy's highest decision-making body, the Board of Directors (Board), holds the overarching responsibility for the overall conduct of our business. The Board is dedicated to promoting responsible and sustainable value creation business activities that align with our shareholder's ambitions and the interests of our key stakeholders. With their extensive and deep experience, our board members bring context and focus to relevant sustainability issues and hold leadership and senior advisory roles across the international energy, and investment sectors, represented by current and past senior executives from Mubadala Investment Company, and CEPSA. Members of the Board are appointed directly by Mubadala Energy' s shareholder, and a periodic evaluation is conducted by our shareholder to ensure the right expertise is in place for overseeing, among other things, the prudent management of sustainability and ESG considerations, and their associated impacts. In terms of diversity metrics, we have representation of both male and female industry leaders on the Board, and the percentage of independent Board members has almost doubled over the last three years. The diverse international expertise and skillsets of our Board provides the right focus and engagement on how Mubadala Energy can adopt and integrate leading industry practices within our business and help to shape our strategic focus, in line with the shareholder's priorities. Regular Board meetings were held throughout 2023, wherein sustainability-related issues are discussed. The Board has the purview of our progress on implementing the Mubadala Energy sustainability strategy, which was launched in 2022. Furthermore, ESG due diligence conducted for our portfolio optimization activities, which include new investments or divestiture decisions, are presented to the Board. In 2024, we are working towards institutionalizing this ESG due diligence process within our Investment Lifecycle process. We also actively strive to engage with our Board members on our sustainability reporting. Aligned with this, our Board members were engaged April 2024 in the annual refresh of our Materiality Assessment (see page 15 for the results). We believe that clear frameworks and policies must be upheld and enforced by everyone who works for, or with our company, including our business partners. This is the foundation for our Ethics and Compliance Program, which has received ISO 37001 certification. - Code of Ethics: sets forward the foundational principles, standards and behaviors required to achieve our ambitions and uphold our values. It goes beyond baseline compliance with regulatory requirements to reflect our endeavor to operate at the highest levels of integrity and business conduct. - Business Partner Code of Conduct: sets forth the minimum expectations for the conduct of our business partners who are engaging in work for, or on behalf of Mubadala Energy, whether they may be contractors, subcontractors, consultants, etc. - Anti-bribery and Corruption Policy: underpins our commitment against all forms of bribery and corruption and regulates the offering and receiving of gifts, entertainment, sponsorship, and hospitality from and to our personnel. - Conflict of Interest Policy: stipulates disclosure requirements for specific situations of conflict of interest whereby employees are required to proactively disclose such instances for resolution and management. - Personal Trading Policy: provides guidance to employees in recognizing market misconduct, how to avoid it, how and when to complete required disclosures related to personal Securities trading activities - International Trade Controls: sets the framework for understanding the legal and regulatory requirements applicable to international trade transactions. - Data Privacy: sets minimum expectations to ensure that we adopt good practices when handling personal and private data. - To learn more about these policies, please visit here www.mubadalaenergy.com Every year, we carry out employee training in the Code of Ethics and deliver risk-based training and engagement sessions to specific groups, as well as through employee town-halls. In our Malaysia and Indonesia operations, we also conduct an annual Southeast Asia Ethics and Compliance Roadshow. In 2023, 100% of employees completed annual online training and refresher course, demonstrating our unwavering commitment to upholding our values and instilling them in our culture. Business resilience and financial sustainability are core foundations of our approach to growing our business and creating value for our stakeholders. We aim to contribute to meeting the ever-increasing global energy demand through responsibly investing in commercially resilient projects. Our priority is to ensure that we remain relevant and competitive, by focusing on developing a balanced portfolio of investments across the value chain that reflects our strategic view of the energy markets.

We adhere to our Operations Management System (OMS) to drive our operations. Our OMS is designed to foster a culture of preventing all unsafe acts and conditions while streamlining processes and procedures to achieve the highest level of efficiency in day-to-day operations. It covers all aspects related to operational functions, including HSSE and asset integrity management (AIM), exploration, digital data management, subsurface, drilling, production, and engineering and projects. From an environmental perspective, the OMS also guides our efforts towards proactively identifying and mitigating potential environmental risks, including GHG emissions and other air pollutants, waste management, water and energy use, and biodiversity impacts. The OMS, and our Environmental Management Standards (EMS) are governed by our QHSSE Policy. In 2023, the EMS in our Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia business units are certified to ISO 14001: Environmental Management, ISO 9001: Quality Management, and ISO 45001: Occupational Health and Safety Management. Our assurance process is comprehensive, including internal and external audits, trend analysis, investigations, compliance reports, lessons learned, and assessment of our performance against Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Via our internal audit process, we assess compliance with targeted operational requirements, ensuring that policies, standards, and procedures are efficiently executed and maintained throughout the lifecycle of our projects. Through these measures, we continuously improve and ensure that we are meeting the highest standards of safety, quality, and efficiency.

To ensure the integrity of all Mubadala Energy assets throughout their life cycle, an Asset Integrity Management (AIM) Standard forms part of the OMS. It focuses on establishing and maintaining appropriate procedures for start-up, operations, maintenance and shutdown of facilities, with particular attention to critical equipment, systems and processes. All business units are mandated to undertake an annual independent AIM review to provide extra assurance that asset integrity is effectively managed. Alongside our AIM Standard, we have several other supporting standards and procedures that guide our activities: - Functional Safety Standard - Safety Critical Element Standard - Safe System of Work Standard - Operational Risk Management Standard - Management of Change Standard A Risk Management Protocol prioritizes equipment based on safety and business criticality. Safetycritical equipment and elements are managed in accordance with specific performance criteria to ensure their functionality in the event of an emergency. In addition, any degradation to equipment, plant, process lines, structural components, pipelines, etc. are identified, assessed and mitigated. To prevent major process safety incidents, failure modes and root causes are thoroughly understood through established tools such as failure modes and effects / root cause analysis. The impact of equipment failure is considered in overall system reliability, and enhanced inspection and maintenance are established for equipment whose failure could impact system reliability. By adhering to these protocols, we ensure that all assets operate with integrity and that risks are minimized throughout the equipment's life cycle.

2023 continued to be a volatile year for energy markets, with geopolitical tensions, producer interventions, environmental concerns and energy cost considerations to consumers all issues that played a dominant role. However, despite this backdrop, Mubadala Energy continued its focused approach to responsible value creation, and our efforts have borne fruit. Our working interest production in 2023 averaged ca. 369,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, which reflected the ramp up of gas production in our Pegaga gas field in Malaysia, balanced by the finalization of our operated oil assets' divestment in Thailand at the end of Q1. 2023 was also a pivotal year of success for Mubadala Energy, as we announced the success of our Layaran-1 exploration wells, in Indonesia's South Andaman acreage which we operate. This has the potential to play an important role in Indonesia's energy markets.

This required additional involvement to prepare the Company for the introduction of the new law. Against this backdrop, Mubadala Energy remained committed to financial stability, underpinned by our sustainability efforts to grow our business and create value for our stakeholders. With global demand for energy continuing to increase, we aim to help meet needs by investment in responsible and resilient projects. We focus on developing a balanced portfolio of investments across the value chain that reflects our strategic view of the energy markets. Our business plan is designed to take account of a range of global economic forecasts whilst retaining the ability to take advantage of opportunities with the appropriate downside protections in place. In 2023, active cost monitoring and exercising extension options in long-term contracts for better rates than prevailing market rates helped us navigate the inflationary environment. Overall, we achieved 25% savings in operating costs and 45% savings in capital expenditure, which allowed us to meet and exceed our financial targets in terms of EBITDA, Net Income and Net Cash delivery to our shareholder.

Since 2020, Mubadala Energy has worked to enhance its corporate governance and control environment of its financial information for greater transparency and to help prevent the risk of misstatement. Through implementing Internal Controls over Financial Reporting, as well as aligning to the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) framework, we ensure following a comprehensive financial approach that fulfills Abu Dhabi Accountability Authority' s (ADAA) requirements. We utilize several governance controls such as our Tender Committee, Finance Committees for each asset, our Audit Risk and Compliance Committee, and the Audit Review Committee, to ensure transparency in our practices. We are in dialogue with the relevant Revenue Departments and Ministries of Finance in the respective countries and disclose relevant information as required. We have global financial governance policies in place, cascaded and embedded in our Enterprise Resource Planning system to ensure compliance with policies, procedures, and authority limits. Policies and procedures are reviewed annually across all Mubadala Energy's finance departments to ensure that there are no gaps in controls and that all new processes are updated and documented. Mubadala Energy conducts rigorous internal audits based on risk managed by our shareholder to ensure independence as per The Institute of Internal Auditors requirements. Establishing and maintaining a secure environment for the protection of Mubadala Energy's data is essential to the healthy operations of our business. We are proud to hold ISO/IEC 27001 certification for our UAE, Malaysia, and Indonesia operated locations. This is an integral part of our commitment to complying with leading international standards for information security, confirming that we have sufficient controls in place to protect all processes related to information security and data workflows. To effectively manage security risks, we consistently identify, assess, report, and rectify vulnerabilities. This involves leveraging critical risk assessments and real-time threat intelligence. In addition, we regularly review and enhance our security controls to address any identified gaps. Our IT team has developed clear security policies and procedures, updated annually, governing data and system operations. These include manuals and policies including our Information Security Management System, Cloud Security, Threat Intelligence, Security Operations, and procedures for Vulnerability. Our Information Security Incident Management procedure requires employees to report any suspicious cybersecurity activities to IT service desk or the Information Security team. This procedure outlines the requirements for managing and responding to information security incidents to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of company information assets, information systems, and networks. Vulnerabilities such as unpatched software, phishing and misconfigurations are regularly monitored and evaluated to understand the threats that are most likely to affect the company. In our 2023 ISO/IEC 27001 audit, we successfully maintained compliance with no observations or non-conformities. While we have avoided data security breaches, we maintain a well-prepared and structured plan for any incidents that may arise. If a breach is suspected, our Incident Response Plan is instantly activated, with our Incident Response Team coordinating response efforts. Measures are swiftly taken to contain the breach and prevent further access, and all evidence is preserved to support any current or future investigations. Breaches will be investigated thoroughly, and we will learn from the incident to both fix the system and bolster our security for the future. Given our global presence, it is important that we implement standardized internal procedures and processes in coherence with Mubadala's Information Management Policy. We have therefore established an Information Management Forum, led by the Information Technology Director, to create information registers and define retention schedules for handling information in a compliant manner throughout its entire life cycle. Our current focus is on implementing solutions to reinforce relevant policies in Microsoft-based document management platforms. Finally, we have a robust data privacy program, aligned with regulatory requirements including the European Union General Data Protection Regulation and UAE's Personal Data Protection law. Our current focus is on implementing identified tools and management systems to ensure compliance with the policy requirements. In 2023, our annual IT Disaster Recovery test showed a 100% success rate across all global geographies.

We also participated in a data privacy audit conducted by our shareholder. We took a number of actions, including enhancing our data privacy governance framework, enhancing classification labeling review programs, conducting regular reviews and updates of data retention schedules, and implementing standardized third-party data protection clauses for exchanging personal information. As the global energy industry shifts towards a more sustainable future, companies are recognizing the need to embrace digital technologies to drive innovation. Three years into the implementation of our Digital Transformation Strategy, we are beginning to see results against our mission to foster a digital culture that supports sustainable value and accelerates the path to energy transition. In 2023, we rolled out the identity for our digital transformation journey - E-VOLVE geared at accelerating the execution of our transformation projects. Aligned with our business goals, the introduction of E-VOLVE strengthens our commitment to operational efficiency and innovation. As we navigate the evolving digital landscape, embracing E-VOLVE remains essential for our future success, ensuring positive change and sustained value creation for shareholders and partners through digital solutions.

In 2019, we launched our Digital Transformation roadmap to cultivate a digital culture that supports the company's objective to deliver sustainable value and accelerate our path to energy transition. Alongside our Digital Transformation Strategy, our Information Technology Strategy is aimed at areas such as process optimization, cyber resilience, people development, cloud excellence, data management, and advanced analytics. - Digital Operating Model was mobilized, including the implementation of a digital opportunities identification system and a portfolio dashboard, and the activation of a dedicated Digital Champions Network to enhance our opportunity identification processes. - HSSE Tracking Dashboard was introduced, including the implementation of video/sensor analytics and alerting systems, and real time GHG emissions measurement and monitoring systems. content_text: At Mubadala Energy, we manage risks that are related to our strategy and its execution. We administer a structured risk assessment process to identify all applicable enterprise risks and risk factors that are relevant for our industry and geographies. Governed by our Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Standard, we continue working towards actioning a comprehensive Risk Management Framework which ensures the accurate identification, mitigation and management of potential risks that could negatively impact our business and its operations.

Each business unit and function throughout the Mubadala Energy portfolio conducts the ERM process at minimum, on a quarterly basis. At the corporate level, risks are then consolidated to provide our Mubadala Energy leadership with clear oversight of the overall risk landscape to which the company is exposed. This risk information will inform decision-making and provide assurance that risks are identified and managed across the organization. A key element of our risk management structures includes the appointment of Risk Champions, who work together to identify mitigating controls in place and develop additional risk mitigation plans according to the type of risk and resources available that are necessary to reduce the risk's residual impact. The ERM function regularly engages with risk owners and champions with both one-to-one sessions and workshops; such engagement supports the effective development of the company's risk culture, in addition to regular risk awareness communications and direct risk reporting to all employees. Moreover, the ERM function participates in operational performance review meetings for all operated and non-operated assets. To continue enhancing our risk management practices, we conducted a major review of our ERM Standard in 2023, which captured lessons learned, improvement opportunities and enhanced alignment with the expectations of our shareholder. The revised ERM Standard which has now been implemented reflects best practices in the industry. In the future, we aim to further align our ERM policies with international standards such as ISO 31000, and to continue raising awareness about ERM through conducting more frequent risk workshops with our asset managers, functions, and business units.

Our established Emissions Management Committee coordinates and directs initiatives focused on exploring opportunities for GHG emissions reduction and optimization across the portfolio. To ensure that risks are identified and to support decision-making, risks are consolidated to provide our Mubadala Energy leadership with a comprehensive view of the overall risk landscape. The ExCom has oversight and is part of the approvals hierarchy of our business planning, which includes initiatives in decarbonizing our portfolio, and where applicable, capital allocation on investments in low carbon solutions. The Committee's recommendations led to the enhancement of the decarbonization roadmap, ensuring that both energy transition and physical risks were addressed. 1. GHG Data Reporting Period: The reporting period for GHG data covers the calendar year, commencing on 1 January and concluding on 31 December. 2. Reporting Boundaries and Operational Control: GHG reporting boundaries are determined based on the concept of 'Operational Control' . This approach defines the scope of reporting responsibilities and the operational influence the organization has over its assets. 3. Methodology: Each asset within the defined reporting boundaries must identify all sources of GHG emissions, categorized as Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions. The raw data collected from each asset is reported to the relevant Business Unit either daily or monthly, as appropriate. This data undergoes calculation and conversion according to the company's internal guidelines, which reference the applicable emission factors derived from local regulatory guidelines and international standards and guidelines. The GHG emissions data from each Business Unit are then consolidated and reported to the corporate office on a monthly basis, which produces a comprehensive companywide GHG emissions report. This report, presented in the company's Sustainability Report, includes emissions data in terms of the mass of CO2 e (carbon dioxide equivalent) or intensity metrics.
